text:
[LCST.4.5.7] **`String → Int` accepted inputs.** `x::Int?` parses a string that
is, in its entirety, an optional sign (`+` or `-`) followed by an `INT_LIT`
([LLEX.11.1]): decimal, `0x` hexadecimal, `0b` binary or `0o` octal, with `_`
separators placed as a source literal may place them. The runtime must yield
the signed value when it lies in the 64-bit range, and `null` for every other
string: one outside that range, one with any surrounding whitespace, a decimal
point or exponent, a unit suffix, or any spelling a source `INT_LIT` would not
admit.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__accepted_spellings
idris.note: The positive fixture's eight texts, executed, each to 31 or -31.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__digit
idris.note: One digit of a base, or nothing.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__digits_run
idris.note: The digits after the first, a `_` only where a source literal places one: before a digit ([LLEX.12.1]).

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__in_range
idris.note: The 64-bit range: a value inside it stands; one outside it is nothing -- `null`, not a saturated value and not a fault.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__leading_space_and_empty_are_null
idris.note: Surrounding whitespace: a leading space is `null` for every tail, and so is the empty text.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__parse_int
idris.note: `String :: Int?`: the whole text an optional sign then an `INT_LIT` ([LLEX.11.1]), the signed value when it lies in the 64-bit range and nothing -- `null`, through `lnul_8_4__parsed` -- for every other text.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__parse_is_a_value_or_null
idris.note: For every text, `s :: Int?` is an Int or `null`, the clause's two answers, never a trap.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__refused_spellings
idris.note: The negative fixture's spellings executed to `null`: `31.0`, `3e1`, `31 `, `31_s`, `31s`, `0x_1F`, `_31`, `31_`, `0X1F`, `0x1G`; the out-of-range magnitudes are run in Main.idr.
